appendText.text: REV 23 SECTION C (SPIKE-FS evidence, PARTIAL): the macOS observation statfs type 25 is a RAM-BACKED HFS+ volume (hdiutil ram:// plus diskutil eraseVolume HFS+); macOS has NO tmpfs, so this is not tmpfs evidence and must never be reported as such. Type 25 is NOT ADMITTED on any root - an id outside the admitted per-root set fails closed, exit 18, naming the observed id and path - and is recorded as an observation only. Admission is never granted by observation alone and never by documentation: it requires an owner-intended per-root entry plus the behaviour battery plus a durability argument, and this volume's durability was never measured (and for memory-backed storage would be expected to fail). APFS type 26 remains admitted for darwin exactly as the rev 4 admission table already states (observed on the dev host, re-observed by SPIKE-FS on darwin 25.5.0 for both /tmp and the repository volume, and re-observed by H-8 under both Node 22.19.0 and Node 24.21.0), for the two live Phase 18 roots run/auth and run/plans; darwin is a local/dev platform and the Linux CI root is UNMEASURED. TIGHTENING: the rev 4 Linux row admitting 0xEF53, 0x58465342 and 0x9123683E from documented magic.h constants is WITHDRAWN FROM ADMISSION, because it contradicts this criterion's own no-id-from-a-kernel-header-or-documentation rule; those ids are readmissible only as observed, committed, per-root values from LINUX-01 or a second SPIKE-FS pass on the real runner, and until then pilot execute mode on Linux, including CI, refuses with exit 18 naming the observed id. SPIKE-FS is PARTIAL: F_FULLFSYNC, reboot/power-loss durability, every Linux id and behaviour, ZFS, and the tmpfs-shared-with-ramfs comparison are UNOBSERVED; ZFS stays inadmissible on every root and 18F cannot merge on this evidence. LINUX-01 (ba8421d, rev 23 section E) now supplies observed Linux ids from digest-pinned Docker Desktop: overlay 0x794c7630, tmpfs 0x1021994, ext4 volume 0xef53, virtiofs 0x6a656a63, with the full behaviour battery PASS on every root under Node 22.19.0 and 24.21.0 on arm64 and amd64. Admission consequence: tmpfs 0x1021994 is ADMITTED for run/auth and run/plans ONLY (no durability claim) and stays REFUSED for an approval/audit root (exit 18, approvals_root_not_durable); overlayfs and virtiofs are NOT admitted on any root; ext4 0xef53 is an observation only inside a Docker Desktop VM volume and is not admitted; unknown ids still fail closed; the ramfs id is UNOBSERVED so the tmpfs-shared-with-ramfs question stays open and is an explicit residual of the tmpfs admission; ZFS stays inadmissible; F_FULLFSYNC and power-loss durability remain untested. Docker Desktop is NOT the GitHub Actions ubuntu x64 runner, which remains REQUIRED and UNMEASURED, so 18F cannot merge.

The checker asserts its own fixture directory against that table - both count and id set - and fails on any extra, missing or duplicate id. Criterion counts are unchanged at 98/89/6/3.
Plus rev 23 section D rule C3.10 and the rev 23 section D.4 printing of table C6-T (27 inversion fixtures, 5 positive controls), which supersedes the rev 21 and rev 22 printed copies.

REV 23 SECTION D: rule C3.10 is added to the same check (DEP0190, measured on Node 24.21.0 and absent on Node 22.19.0 in H-8): in production-reachable scope (C3.7) a spawn/spawnSync call identified by binding (C3.4b) with a truthy shell plus a non-empty args array is FORBIDDEN and fails closed, as are the unanalysable forms (non-literal shell, spread or computed options, non-literal args); the same shape on execFile/execFileSync is forbidden on the same rationale, labelled a design assumption because only the spawn/spawnSync warning emission is measured; in test-classified code the shape is a recorded deterministic warning with a committed baseline and never becomes a failure or evidence of absence. CI runs with NODE_OPTIONS unchanged; the checker's OWN process treats an observed DEP0190 warning as a failure of its own run, and if that in-process observation is infeasible the dynamic check is recorded NOT IMPLEMENTED, never green. Fixture ids and counts come from the rev 23 section D.4 printing of table C6-T: 27 inversion fixtures and 5 positive controls.
Plus rev 23 section D rule C3.10 with fixtures X26 and X27 and positive controls P4 and P5, from the rev 23 section D.4 printing of table C6-T.

set.state: EXECUTED and reported in docs/phase-18-spike-w-findings.md: BLOCKER FOUND. MEASURED on Playwright 1.64.0 / Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (macOS arm64, 3 reps, two runs, no flake): BrowserContext.route() does NOT observe a SharedWorker-initiated fetch (the request reached the loopback fixture and mutated it every repetition); page.on('worker') does NOT fire for a SharedWorker; context.addInitScript() does NOT execute in worker global scope (marker present on window, absent on self inside the worker); dedicated-worker traffic IS interceptable (fetch, sync XHR, importScripts, own script load, EventSource, nested workers, blob:, data:, {type:'module'}), so no dedicated-worker refusal is required on the pinned pair. CONSEQUENCE: the rev 3 claim that SharedWorker is treated as a dedicated worker by the same handler is FALSE and is superseded, and the rev 4 framing of addInitScript as defence in depth inside workers is corrected - dedicated workers are protected by the route/routeWebSocket network layer ONLY. DESIGN REVISED IN REV 23 SECTION B: SharedWorker construction is blocked in every page realm before page scripts run (non-configurable, non-writable throwing stub installed by context.addInitScript) and every attempt is detected out of page by a signal page code cannot suppress (CDP Target.setAutoAttach with waitForDebuggerOnStart for shared_worker targets, never resumed, closed and detached, plus a run-scoped exposeBinding), refusing the run with PILOT_INTERNAL_ERROR exit 18 reason shared_worker_blocked, with the decisive test assertion being zero requests recorded at the fixture and a zero mutation counter. NOTHING ABOUT THAT MECHANISM IS MEASURED. SPIKE-W2 IS REQUIRED BEFORE 18C MERGES and until every one of its cases is recorded MEASURED-PASS the pilot REFUSES TO ARM execute mode (exit 18, reason shared_worker_block_unverified). Carried-forward gaps: data: and module worker cases were corroborated by outcome pattern rather than a route-hit counter; request.frame() identity on a worker-initiated request is only known not to throw; worker-initiated WebSocket was never measured. Environment-dependent observations, not Falcon controls: navigator.sendBeacon is absent in dedicated-worker scope, new Worker(crossOriginUrl) throws synchronously by browser policy, and a route armed after worker creation still applies to that worker's later requests.

appendText.text: EXECUTED PARTIALLY and reported in docs/phase-18-spike-fs-findings.md: PARTIAL. Measured on macOS (darwin 25.5.0, arm64, Node v22.19.0): APFS statfs type 26 on both /tmp and the repository volume, and a RAM-backed HFS+ volume at type 25, with O_EXCL (single and 20-way contention), same-directory rename, file fsync(2), directory fsync, cross-process lock visibility, symlink lstat/O_NOFOLLOW/swap-observability, 0600/0700 permissions under a restrictive umask and the SIGKILL leftover-partial-temp property all PASS on both volumes. UNOBSERVED: Darwin F_FULLFSYNC (Node exposes no fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC) without a native addon), reboot/power-loss durability (unmeasurable in-process by design; rev 4 rejects a capability probe as a durability substitute), every Linux id and behaviour (ext4, xfs, btrfs, overlayfs, tmpfs, virtiofs, drvfs - the Docker daemon was not running), ZFS, and whether the platform tmpfs id is shared with ramfs. Per rev 23 section C: type 25 is a RAM-backed HFS+ observation ONLY and is NOT admitted on any root; APFS 26 stays admitted for darwin as the rev 4 table already states; the documentation-derived Linux ids are withdrawn from admission until observed. 18F cannot merge and ZFS stays inadmissible on every root.

PARTIALLY MEASURED and reported in docs/phase-18-h8-node24-findings.md. STATUS: macOS arm64 ONLY; Linux CI UNMEASURED; H-8 is NOT closed. Node 24.21.0 vs Node 22.19.0 on darwin 25.5.0 arm64: the ONLY observed behavioural difference relevant to Phase 18 is DEP0190 - Node 24.21.0 emits [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning for child_process.spawn/spawnSync called with shell:true and a non-empty args array, Node 22.19.0 does not; GitInfo.js's own execFileSync call (shell unset) is unaffected. Identical under both versions: the entire filesystem battery on APFS (statfs type 26 both), the literal-argv and ENOENT child_process checks, exit-code propagation, the 82/82 Babel parse of falcon.js plus all of src/**, and the CLI exit-2/stderr behaviour across pipe, file redirect and pseudo-TTY with no truncation. NOT MEASURED: Linux/ubuntu x64 anything (filesystem, child_process, DEP0190 presence, the real GitHub Actions runner), Playwright Chromium launch under Node 24, Darwin F_FULLFSYNC, dotenv file-based load ordering, and node falcon.js --help (skipped as unconfirmable-safe within budget). Rev 23 section D folds DEP0190 into the reachability checker as rule C3.10; rev 23 section E lists the Linux statements rev 24 must update once LINUX-01 reports.

REV 23 SECTION B: partially measured. Dedicated-worker requests ARE interceptable by BrowserContext.route() on the pinned pair (fetch, sync XHR, importScripts, own script load, EventSource, nested, blob:, data:, module), so for dedicated workers this residual narrows to WebSocket and service workers. SharedWorker is NOT interceptable (measured 3/3) and is no longer a documented residual: construction is blocked and any attempt refuses the run (exit 18, shared_worker_blocked). addInitScript is NOT a worker-scope control and may not be cited as one. Worker-initiated WebSocket (dedicated and shared) remains UNMEASURED - SPIKE-W dropped it rather than stubbing a misleading pass - and it keeps execute mode refusing to arm until SPIKE-W2 cases W2-15 and W2-16 pass.

Rev 23 adds no exit code and changes no precedence: the rev 6 order stands, 2 > 3 > 18 > 17 > 16 > 15 > 13 > 12 > 11 > 14 > 10 > 1 > 0. It adds TWO new exit-18 reason codes under PILOT_INTERNAL_ERROR: shared_worker_blocked (a SharedWorker construction was attempted; the run refuses, with the attempted origin and canonical path and the frame identity in the message, and never the query or fragment) and shared_worker_block_unverified (execute mode refuses to ARM because the SPIKE-W2 evidence is absent or incomplete; raised at NetworkGate install time, before any navigation). NAMING, checked against the existing registry: exit-18 reasons in this design are lower snake_case modifiers of PILOT_INTERNAL_ERROR (worker_not_interceptable, approvals_root_not_durable, approvals_root_symlink, approval_history_unverifiable) while POLICY_* is the family of top-level failure codes (POLICY_NETWORK_BLOCKED, POLICY_ORIGIN_DENIED, POLICY_REDIRECT_LIMIT), so the owner's suggested spelling POLICY_SHARED_WORKER_BLOCKED would be inconsistent on both halves; rev 23 uses shared_worker_blocked and flags this as a naming decision the owner may overrule with no behavioural change.
